The key idea: the graph is symmetric, so the turning point sits halfway between the two roots.

how.higher: Higher level asks for it only once in 2015 to 2025: in 2025 it is a 10 mark part on Paper 1 where you complete a table, plot the points and join them.
how.ordinary: Ordinary level asks for it almost every year on Paper 1, usually as a part of its own worth 5 to 20 marks: complete a table, plot the points, join them with a smooth curve, then read values off your graph.

example.question: Draw the graph of $f(x) = x^2 - 4x - 5$ for $-1 \le x \le 5$. Show where it crosses the axes and find its lowest point.

steps.title: Make a table of values
steps.say: Put each value of $x$ into $f(x)$ and write down the answer. Do the squares and brackets one at a time.

lines.text: Do the same for $x = 2, 3, 4, 5$. The table gives $0, -5, -8, -9, -8, -5, 0$ for $x = -1$ to $5$.

steps.title: Find where it crosses the x-axis
steps.say: The graph crosses the $x$-axis where $f(x) = 0$. Set $f(x)$ equal to $0$ and factorise.

steps.title: Find the lowest point
steps.say: A parabola is symmetric. Its turning point is halfway between the roots $\hl{1}{-1}$ and $\hl{1}{5}$. Find the $\hl{2}{x}$ value, then put it into $f(x)$ for the $\hl{3}{y}$ value.

lines.text: The $x^2$ term is positive, so the curve opens up and this is a minimum.

steps.title: Plot and join
steps.say: Plot the points from the table. Mark the roots $(-1, 0)$ and $(5, 0)$, the $y$-intercept $(0, -5)$ and the minimum $(\hl{2}{2}, \hl{3}{-9})$. Join them with one smooth curve, not straight lines.

lines.text: Use a pencil and draw the curve through every point.

example.question: Draw the graph of $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x$ for $-1 \le x \le 4$. Find the local maximum point.

steps.title: Make a table of values
steps.say: Put each value of $x$ into $f(x)$. Take care with the signs when $x$ is negative.

steps.title: Find the turning points
steps.say: The turning points are where the slope is zero. Differentiate, set $f'(x)$ equal to $0$ and solve.

lines.text: Every term divides by 3. Do that first.

steps.title: Find the maximum
steps.say: The curve rises, then falls. So the first turning point, at $x = \hl{1}{1}$, is the maximum. Put it into $f(x)$ for the $y$ value.

lines.text: The local maximum is at $(1, 4)$ and the local minimum is at $(3, 0)$.

steps.title: Plot and join
steps.say: Plot the points from the table, with the turning points $(\hl{1}{1}, \hl{2}{4})$ and $(3, 0)$ among them. Join them with one smooth curve.

say: You give it an exponential, $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$. It draws the curve, which starts at $(0, a)$ and then climbs faster and faster.
The key idea: each step of $1$ in $x$ multiplies $y$ by $b$, and the curve never touches the $x$-axis.

how.ordinary: Ordinary level asks for it in 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2025 on Paper 1: complete a table (5 to 10 marks), plot and join the points, then use the graph or the formula to answer a question about growth.

example.question: The number of bacteria is $f(x) = 5 \cdot 2^x$, where $x$ is the number of hours. Draw the graph of $f$ for $-1 \le x \le 4$. Use the graph to find when there are $40$ bacteria.

steps.title: Make a table of values
steps.say: Put each value of $x$ into $5 \cdot 2^x$. A negative power means one over the positive power.

steps.title: Plot and join
steps.say: Plot the points from the table. Join them with a smooth curve that rises more steeply to the right and gets very close to the $x$-axis on the left, but does not touch it.

lines.text: The curve crosses the $y$-axis at $(0, 5)$, the value of $a$.

steps.title: Read the graph
steps.say: To find when there are $40$ bacteria, go across from $40$ on the $y$-axis to the curve, then down to the $x$-axis. Check it with the equation.

lines.text: The curve reads $x = 3$ at $f(x) = \hl{2}{40}$. After $3$ hours there are $40$ bacteria.

say: You give it two functions, $f(x)$ and $g(x)$. It builds the **composite** $f(g(x))$: put $g$ in first, then $f$.
The key idea: wherever $f$ has an $x$, write the whole of $g(x)$ in brackets instead.

how.higher: Higher level uses it in most years on Paper 1 (2017, 2020, 2023, 2024, 2025). It is the main skill of a 10 mark part in 2020 (show $f(g(x)) = x$) and 2024 (find $g(f(x))$), and a step inside longer parts in the other years.

example.question: $f(x) = x + 2$ and $g(x) = x^2 - 3$. Find $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$. Hence find the value of $x$ for which $f(g(x)) = g(f(x))$.

steps.title: Put g inside f
steps.say: For $f(g(x))$, take $g(x) = x^2 - 3$ and put it into $f$ wherever there is an $x$.

steps.title: Put f inside g
steps.say: For $g(f(x))$, take $f(x) = x + 2$ and put it into $g$ wherever there is an $x$. Square the whole bracket.

lines.text: The two composites are not the same. Order matters.

steps.title: Set them equal
steps.say: Set $\hl{1}{f(g(x))}$ equal to $\hl{2}{g(f(x))}$. The $x^2$ terms cancel, which leaves a linear equation.

higher.tip: To show two functions undo each other, work out both $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$ and simplify each to $x$. One composition alone is only part of the answer, and checking one number earns little.
